key_insight: Pre-implantation kidney biopsy results add only a small overall prognostic boost, but combining continuous histology scores with donor risk indices reveals more informative risk patterns for graft outcomes.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help transplant teams better identify which higher-risk deceased-donor kidneys may still be usable and which have compounded injury risk.
method: 733 deceased-donor kidney biopsies were processed under optimized lab conditions and digitized as whole-slide images.
Expert Banff 2024 pathology assessment was paired with BanffNET deep-learning quantification of 17 histologic lesions.
Researchers tested incremental prediction for graft dysfunction, eGFR/UPCR trajectories, indication biopsies, and death-censored graft failure.
evidence_signal: Compared with clinical models alone, histology improved discrimination by about 1–4% and explained variance for longitudinal outcomes by about 1–2%, with stronger insight from continuous KDRI–BanffNET risk surfaces.
watch_item: The study shows modest average prediction gains, so real-world benefit may depend on consistent biopsy processing, digital pathology infrastructure, and careful validation before adoption.
paper_title: Validation of the Incremental Prognostic Value of Deceased Donation Pre-implantation Kidney Transplant Biopsies through Comprehensive Lesion Quantification with Deep Learning
